function: Predicts downlink CSI of high-mobility multi-antenna users from partial, stale uplink CSI (CGAN infills missing antennas, LSTM predicts); also outputs precoding matrices directly. p. 1, p. 3
system: TDD massive MIMO, one cell; BS M=128 antennas (64 and 256 also tested), K=10 users with N=4 antennas; 2 GHz, 20 MHz; no RIS. p. 9-10
method: CGAN (U-shaped convolutional encoder-decoder generator) plus LSTM, supervised on pairs of partial and complete CSI, trained separately with Adam, 40 epochs. p. 5, p. 7, p. 9
data_channel: Own simulator: spatially and temporally correlated Rayleigh fading (AR model); UMi NLoS large-scale fading from 3GPP TR 36.814; 500 training and 100 test episodes. p. 3, p. 9
test_conditions: Training and test episodes drawn from the same simulator (500 and 100; 2-4 of 10 users partial, 30-50 km/h); missing-CSI amount and M swept. p. 9-10
baselines: Non-learned: method of [23] (neighbouring-antenna mean), stale and mean infilling, complete MMSE CSI bound. Learned: DNN of [18], transformer of [22]. p. 10-11
metrics: NMSE of CSI (CGAN alone and full scheme); DL sum spectral efficiency (bits/s/Hz) with MF and BD precoding; training-loss convergence. p. 9, p. 11-14
complexity: FLOPs analysis: CGAN O(M^2 P) naive, O(MKNP) with sparse input; LSTM O(KPU^2+MKNPU); parameters LSTM 1.8M, transformer 2.1M, DNN 6.05M. p. 8, p. 11
openness: none; the only open-source code mentioned is another author's repository for [50], used to develop the simulations. p. 15
q1_support: p. 3: "We assume the channels undergo spatially- and temporally-correlated Rayleigh fading." Custom AR-Rayleigh simulator; only the large-scale fading follows 3GPP TR 36.814 (p. 9: "we follow the urban microcell non-line-of-sight (UMi NLoS) model in [56]"; [56] is listed on p. 16). No TR 38.901, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 15: "could examine how well our proposed CGAN-LSTM scheme adapts to environmental changes and/or transfers its learning to different environments" (left as future work). Test data are independent episodes of the same simulator (p. 9: "500 and 100 independent episodes"); the Fig. 5 sweep on p. 10 does not say the model is trained once and tested on another configuration.
q3_support: p. 10: "we consider the DNN model consisting of fully-connected layers from [18] and the transformer model from [22]"; p. 11: "the method adapted from [23] does not use ML". All are compared on NMSE (Fig. 6, p. 11) and on sum SE (Fig. 8, pp. 12-13); stale and mean infilling are further non-learned baselines.
q4_support: p. 8: "with a coefficient of about 184209 on the highest order term" (CGAN O(M^2 P) FLOPs; LSTM O(KPU^2+MKNPU)); p. 11: "the transformer we have adapted herein contains about 2.1 million trainable NN parameters, whereas the LSTM network has about 1.8 million".
q5_support: p. 15: "for the open-source code repository for [50] (available at [75]), which helped them to develop their simulations". This is another author's code; the paper releases no code or data of its own and trains on its own simulated channels (p. 9).
notes: Checked: p. 1 holds the title and DOI 10.1109/TWC.2024.3485128. Area 2 because the main metric is the NMSE of CSI prediction and estimation; the direct precoding output is an extension judged by sum SE. q1 is borderline: only the UMi NLoS large-scale fading comes from 3GPP TR 36.814 (LTE, ref. [56]), small-scale fading is a custom AR-Rayleigh model. Baselines: [23] Qian et al., [18] Kim et al., [22] Jiang et al. (p. 15).
